label: soco 1 baseline
definition: THE FIRST SOCO KEEPER. DETERMINATION NOT-YET (rubric v3.8, PRICE UNSCORED). SOCO has no public price and never will: no actual_lmp.json block exists, so C3a / C3b / C3c are UNSCORABLE — not failed — and this run is scored on C1 / C2 / C4 / C6 / C8 only. The ceiling is PHYSICALLY-CALIBRATED (PRICE UNSCORED); it can never read CALIBRATED. THE RECIPE is the CLI's all-defaults ISO-agnostic backcast construction — no --set, no --offer-curve-json, no floor, share, threshold or adder set by this lane — on three geographic zones (SOCO_AL / SOCO_GA / SOCO_MS) over measured FERC-714 shares from the five fully-cited respondents, Tier-3 non-binding links, served measured EIA-930 interchange, VOLL 61,900. Every offer_curve_by_group band is exactly 1.0 on all 13 groups and authorized_price_tuning is declared NONE. COAL IS SPLIT TO COAL_BIT / COAL_PRB on the measured EIA-923 supply census (owner instruction, verbatim: "Coal should be split into types. Completely eliminate the single coal class.") — every year carries both classes and no bare COAL. SCORED: C1 FAIL on ONE row of fourteen (2023 CT_PEAKER +8.221 TWh, share +3.4pp); C2 PASS, C4 PASS, C6 PASS, C8 PASS (0.0 % forced on every material merchant class); 0 ledgered and 0 protective caveats. The coal split cut C1's failing rows from SEVEN to ONE and every coal row now passes — 2024 COAL_BIT lands at 12.256 against 12.257 actual. THE ONE OPEN DEFECT is the CT_PEAKER / ST_GAS merit-order split: CT_PEAKER runs +8.221 / +4.933 / +7.867 TWh while ST_GAS runs -6.487 / -4.996 / -4.584, a near-offsetting misallocation and SOCO's first lever. 2025 additionally carries an EIA-923 hydro INPUT hole named before the solve (5 plants / 0.327 TWh against 6.012 measured), which coal backfills and which posts 8,930 MWh of VOLL slack in 13 summer afternoon hours. Determination basis, DOF ledger (3 entries, 1 residual) and all eight disclosures: results/calibration/soco40_coalsplit_B/calibration_attestation.json and docs/handoffs/FINDING-soco-40-2026-09-16.md.
market_story: Southern Company is a vertically-integrated, energy-only footprint with no organized market, no capacity market, no ancillary-service market and no published price. Dispatch is a cost-based merit order across ~250 TWh/yr: a very large gas CC fleet (~110 TWh) carries base and mid-merit, nuclear runs flat at ~52-64 TWh and steps up twice in this span as Vogtle 3 (2023-07) and Vogtle 4 (2024-04) come online, coal follows gas prices on a plant-specific delivered-fuel basis split between Powder River Basin (Miller, Daniel, Scherer) and Appalachian bituminous (Barry, Gaston, Bowen), and the system exports 10-13 TWh/yr to nine neighbouring BAs. The model reproduces that ordering: gas and coal volumes land inside C2's band in every year, hourly dispatch correlates with the measured fleet, and nothing is forced — 0.0 % of every material merchant class's energy sits at a binding floor, the only floors being nuclear must-run and CHP steam host duty. What it does NOT yet reproduce is the split WITHIN the peaking fleet: the LP sends energy to combustion turbines that the real system sent to gas steam units, in near-equal and opposite amounts. Because SOCO publishes no price, none of this is or can be validated on price — the model's own mean LMP is reported MODEL-ONLY and UNVERIFIED.
